snippets.title: Windows on Arm overview
snippets.summary: Windows 11 supports ARM64 natively and emulates x64; native ARM64 unlocks best performance and battery.

snippets.title: Arm64EC overview
snippets.summary: Arm64EC lets one process mix native ARM64 code with x64 modules under emulation, enabling incremental migration.

snippets.title: Add Arm support to your Windows app
snippets.summary: Four-stage workflow (assess, plan, build, validate) for adding ARM64 support to an existing Windows app.

snippets.title: Platform-specificity of Python packages on Windows on Arm
snippets.section: Native wheels, source builds, and repo-level patterns
snippets.summary: Python packages with compiled extensions need win_arm64 wheels; without them pip falls back to source builds requiring MSVC and often Rust.

snippets.title: PyTorch on Windows on Arm — install status and GPU-parity gap
snippets.section: CPU wheels, CUDA gap, DirectML, ONNX fallback
snippets.summary: PyTorch ships CPU-only win_arm64 wheels; CUDA is unavailable on Windows on Arm, so GPU parity requires torch-directml or ONNX Runtime.

snippets.title: GitHub Actions windows-11-arm runner and setup-python on ARM64
snippets.section: CI matrix patterns and common failure modes
snippets.summary: Use runs-on: windows-11-arm with actions/setup-python architecture: arm64; watch for source-build fallbacks and cache-key architecture collisions.

snippets.title: ONNX Runtime on Windows on Arm — the primary native-ARM64 inference path
snippets.summary: ONNX Runtime is the default native-ARM64 inference fallback for CUDA-dependent workloads on Windows on Arm; QNN provider targets Snapdragon X NPUs.
